A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IMMAX research work. The main text, Figure 1, Tables 1–3, equations, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison. The appendices match after accounting for bibliography reflow.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original classification experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet, including ResNet-34 results in Tables 1–2 and binary linear-model results in Table 3.

after.justification: v3 retains the original multiclass and binary classification experiments and their reported accuracies and standard deviations in Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: The binary and multiclass IMMAX objectives, class-dependent confidence margins, regularization, and margin-selection procedures in Sections 4–5 and Appendices D–F are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate long-tailed and step-imbalanced CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet, plus airplane, automobile, and horse versus the remaining CIFAR-10 classes. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain CE, RW, BS, EQUAL, LA, CB, FOCAL, and LDAM as comparators; Table 3 retains HINGE and LDAM. Newly cited works do not participate in the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 7 retains the same imbalanced training/test construction, accuracy metric, imbalance ratios of 10, 100, and 200, ResNet-34 configuration, 200-epoch training, and cross-validation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 1 retains the same separable-data illustration comparing decision boundaries. No ablation, robustness, sensitivity, or error-analysis evidence is added or removed in the main text or appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run means and standard deviations in Section 7 and Tables 1–2, with the same uncertainty format in Table 3. Run-count information and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All result entries and rankings in Tables 1–3 match, as do Figure 1 and the reported qualitative findings. For example, Table 1 retains IMMAX's TinyImageNet accuracy of 65.20 ± 0.65 at long-tailed imbalance ratio 200.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, H-consistency theorems, generalization bounds, cost-sensitive Bayes-inconsistency result, and derivations and proofs in Appendices C–F are unchanged. Added citations in Section 2 introduce no new mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims about the class-imbalanced margin loss, consistency and generalization guarantees, IMMAX algorithms, and empirical advantages. Their scope and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanation of contrasting margin recommendations in Section 6 and the applicability qualifications in Sections 7–8 are unchanged. Both retain the discussion of balanced-loss objectives, margin tuning, scalability, and temperature scaling.

D1.justification: Section 7 and Appendix B retain the same augmentation, optimizer, batch size, weight decay, learning-rate schedule, and hyperparameter search ranges. No implementation details or code/data access information are added or revised.

R1.justification: v3 adds eight cited works: Cortes et al. (2025) on balanced classification, DeSalvo et al. (2025), Mohri and Zhong (2025), and five Montreuil et al. works. These expand citations in Sections 1–2 and Appendix A without substantive changes to comparative discussion or research positioning.

P1.justification: Citation and bibliography edits include updating the year of Mao et al.'s Enhanced H-consistency bounds from 2024 to 2025 and adjusting author-year suffixes. The substantive prose and section/appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded citation blocks cause local text and equation reflow, particularly on pages 3–4 and in Appendix A, and the bibliography reflows. Figure 1 and Tables 1–3 retain their designs, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: The added references and updated citation year refresh the bibliography without changing or clarifying the scientific argument. The proofs, empirical support, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, leaving overall paper quality essentially the same.
